messages:
sam: Heads up — seeing intermittent 2-3x tail latency spikes when streaming + continuous batching on canary. Spikes align with partial-decode flushes. Anyone else?

maria: saw something similar yesterday on dedicated pools. Usually when batcher flushes half-filled batches for streaming.

josh: can you paste the batcher config and a small profile snippet?

sam: config: `batch_max_tokens=2048, token_budget_target=256, max_batch_latency_ms=12, flush_on_partial_decode=true, queue_policy=priority_time`

sam: profile (token-level summary):
```
> perf: avg_token_latency=6.8ms, p95_token_latency=28ms
> when flush_on_partial_decode triggers: p95_token_latency jumps -> 70-90ms
> cpu: memcpy spikes on decode path, gpu kernels show small kernel launches (~us) more often
> kv-cache: lock hold time ~ 3-5ms on some requests
```

maria: interesting — memcpy spikes suggest more host->device/host traffic when partial decode streams smaller chunks. Could be kernel selection fallback choosing non-batched path for short suffix lengths.

lee: +1. We recently landed kernel selector change (v0.9.3) that prefers single-token kernels below 8-token suffix to reduce kernel overhead. But those kernels do extra memcopies for alignment. Maybe the new policy regresses streaming short-chunk workloads.

josh: so two interacting effects: (1) batch formation/queue policy -> more small batches, (2) kernel selector -> selects memcpy-heavy kernel for small suffixes, (3) KV-cache lock contention when batches overlap partial-decode flushes.

maria: quick mitigation options: reduce flush_on_partial_decode aggressiveness, increase token_budget_target so batches fill more before flush, or introduce a time-based minimum flush window (e.g., min_flush_ms=6) to avoid too-frequent flushes.

sam: we tried increasing token_budget_target to 512 in a canary, p95 decreased but p50 increased slightly. Users reporting smoother streaming but small added latency to earliest tokens.

lee: tradeoff expected. For streaming UX maybe better to tune partial decode scheduling: schedule partial decodes at 1) token-budget threshold OR 2) time window after first byte (whichever first) but suppress kernel-selector fallback for suffixes up to 16 tokens when streaming mode is active.

josh: proposal: implement two coordinated changes and A/B them:
- batching: add adaptive token_budget_target that grows with concurrency (start 256, if avg wait_time>8ms increase to 384/512).
- decoder: add streaming-kernel-hint that biases selector away from memcpy path for live streams (keep batched kernels for suffix<=16).

maria: + add metrics: per-request "partial_flush_count", "avg_partial_chunk_size", "kv_lock_ms", and a label for kernel_variant used. We'll need these for rollback thresholds.

sam: also noticed queue_policy=priority_time tends to favor older requests and creates many small batches under bursty traffic. Maybe try `queue_policy=time_or_count` with min_batch_fill=0.6 to avoid tiny batches.

lee: good call. It might also help GPU utilization and reduce kernel-launch overhead.

josh: timeline? I can prototype a selector flag and add metrics today. Maria can add the batcher adaptive heuristic tomorrow. Sam can run a canary traffic pattern simulating many small streaming clients to compare.

maria: will add the metrics + dashboard panels: per-kernel p50/p95 latency, partial flush distribution, kv lock histogram. Want rollout guard: if p95_token_latency increases >20% for streaming class -> auto rollback.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for selectors/streaming-hint v0.9.4-canary on dedicated-us-west (10% traffic).

sam: test plan for canary:
- synthetic: 1k concurrent streams, average utterance length 32 tokens, inter-token delay 10-50ms
- production: route 5% of streaming API keys to canary with reproducer payloads
- collect new metrics for 60m then evaluate

lee: also add microbench: single-connection partial decode loop to measure memcpy vs batched kernel cost for suffix sizes [1..32]. That will tell us where selector threshold should be.

josh: quick note — KV cache lock: consider sharded per-request locks or optimistic read while decoding to avoid holding global shard lock during host memcpy.

maria: leaving small TODOs in our backlog:
- [ ] slot A: implement streaming-kernel-hint (josh)
- [ ] slot B: adaptive token_budget_target + queue_policy change (maria)
- [ ] slot C: KV lock micro-optimizations (lee)
- [ ] slot D: dashboards + rollback guard (maria)
- [ ] slot E: perf microbench and selector threshold tuning (sam)

sam: thanks — will run the canary and post results here in ~2h. :thumbsup:

josh: thanks — ping if canary shows anything weird, will monitor kernel-variant metrics.

deploy-bot: Canary health update: 1763357060 — no error budget burned, p95_token_latency for streaming class currently -3% vs baseline.

sam: initial canary looks promising. Will keep an eye on kv_lock_ms.

maria: if we see kv_lock spikes later, we should flip the queue_policy back and throttle flush cadence quickly.

sam: noted. Will post final 2h results after the run.
